subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & per-customer routing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & per-customer routing

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have the same priorities and next steps. High level notes below; please let me know if I missed or mis-prioritized anything.

Pain points you mentioned:
- No robust per-tenant rate limiting or fine-grained quotas; current gateway is a blunt instrument (Kong) and is hard to operationalize at scale.
- Need per-customer routing/policies (e.g., route premium customers to higher-capacity model variants or dedicated pools).
- Cost isolation and visibility: finance needs per-tenant token counts and egress estimates.
- Auditability and compliance: per-tenant usage logs, audit trails, and retention controls are required for internal/regulatory audits.

Current stack you shared:
- Self-hosted model endpoints on AWS (EC2/GPU pool)
- Kong API gateway + internal throttles
- Redis for caching / KV
- Homegrown billing extractor for token counts (inaccurate at high throughput)

Success criteria for a POC / pilot:
- Enforce per-customer rate limits and quotas with >95% accuracy for enforcement windows
- Ability to route customers to specific model variants or dedicated pools per policy
- Per-tenant cost/usage visibility and exportable reports for finance
- Audit logs and retention controls for 12+ months (configurable)

Ask / next steps:
1) I'll follow up today with the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a filled SOC2 questionnaire stub — helps speed procurement review. (attached)
2) Technical deep dive with our Solutions Engineer (proposed times next week) to walk through routing, quota semantics, and telemetry collection. Please share two preferred time slots.
3) To scope the pilot pricing/tiering, can you confirm expected peak RPS and target requests/day for pilot (you mentioned ~100k/day)? Also confirm which regions/data residency are must-haves.

Attached: FintechCo_MutualActionPlan.pdf (stub), SOC2_questionnaire_filled_stub.pdf

Thanks — look forward to the next call.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodai.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@fintechco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & per-customer routing

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the summary, that looks right. A few clarifications from my side:

- Pilot size: confirm ~100k requests/day (peak ~15 rps), want to run pilot for 4 weeks with 10 pilot customers.
- SLA ask: we'd like to see options for per-tenant latency SLOs (P95 targets) and an incident escalation path if tenant-level latency degrades.
- Data residency: US only for pilot, but EU is required for our European customers later in the year.
- Cost: finance will need a sample monthly estimate for the pilot (including egress & token estimates) — can you include a simple spreadsheet?

Also: are rate limits enforced at the edge (gateway) or in the Redwood runtime? We need per-tenant hard limits to prevent noisy neighbors; soft throttles won't be enough.

Samira
Director, Platform Ops | FintechCo
samira.k@fintechco.com

Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & per-customer routing (FintechCo)

Marissa / Lauren —

Forwarding Samira's reply and the original recap. Key asks to act on:

1) Technical deep-dive request: Solutions engineering to cover enforcement architecture (edge vs runtime), per-tenant routing policies, and tenant isolation/metrics.
2) Pilot scoping: they want a 4-week pilot with ~10 customers, ~100k req/day. We need a simple cost estimate (RoI_estimate.xlsx) that includes egress & expected token volumes.
3) Compliance / procurement: SOC2 questionnaire attached — procurement will review.

Proposed owner split:
- Marissa: lead the technical deep-dive and prepare a routing/enforcement design doc (include options: gateway-enforced policies vs runtime-enforced quotas, tradeoffs).
- Lauren: own pricing/tiering for pilot and draft the sample monthly estimate for finance.

Notes for the design doc and talking points:
- Redwood supports per-route and per-tenant quotas and hard rate-limit enforcement in the serving runtime; we also expose gateway hooks for enforcement at the edge if customers prefer.
- Routing: support policy rules that map tenant attributes (plan, SLA tier) to model variants or dedicated GPU pools; supports fallbacks when capacity constrained.
- Observability: token-level usage per-tenant, exportable CSVs, tracing hooks, and audit logs with configurable retention.
- Compliance: integrate with KMS for encryption, and produce tenant-scoped audit exports for procurement.

Attachments: RoI_estimate.xlsx (internal stub)

I'll coordinate time slots for the deep-dive — can you both propose 3x 60-min options next week? I'll lock with Samira.

Thanks,
Ben
